prompt: A forecast nearly fills the available six-character code space. Seven-character codes provide much more capacity. Why might the extra character be worth it?

options.text: It leaves room for growth, reserved formats and wasted ID ranges.
options.explanation: Correct. A namespace sized exactly to the forecast can run out earlier when those additional allocations matter.

options.text: It eliminates collisions for randomly generated codes.
options.explanation: A larger space reduces collision risk but does not remove the need for atomic collision handling.

options.text: It makes private links impossible to guess.
options.explanation: Namespace length alone does not establish secrecy; access control or appropriately designed capability tokens are still required.

options.text: It removes the need to retain each code’s destination.
options.explanation: The mapping still has to be stored and recovered regardless of code length.

workedExample: Compare the available values with all allocations you need to preserve, not just successful live links. Reserved names and abandoned ranges consume space. Choose useful headroom, while keeping uniqueness and private access as separate requirements.
